output:
Short answer
- Pick an ENERGY STAR–rated LED task/desk lamp (adjustable arm, dimmable). That combination gives the best balance of energy efficiency, useful light output, and occupant comfort for an office upgrade.
- I see a Meadowlight Lamp in your catalog that could be a candidate, but I don’t have verifiable product specifications in memory — its efficiency claims need to be checked against the spec sheet / ENERGY STAR database.

Why that recommendation
- LEDs use far less power than incandescents/CFLs for the same lumen output and last much longer, so they save energy and replacement costs.
- ENERGY STAR certification (when present) verifies that a lamp meets independent efficiency and performance thresholds for task/desk lighting.
- Dimmable + adjustable arm lets users reduce power/brightness when full output isn’t needed, increasing real-world energy savings and comfort.

What to look for (minimum specs & features)
- ENERGY STAR certification (preferred). Verify on the product spec or the ENERGY STAR product list.
- Lumens per watt (efficacy): higher is better. Aim for at least ~80 lm/W for desk lamps (many good LEDs are 90–120 lm/W).
- Lumens (total output): 400–800 lm for most desk tasks; choose higher for detailed work.
- Correlated color temperature (CCT): 3000–4000 K for office tasks (3000K = warm/relaxed, 4000K = neutral/cooler).
- Color rendering index (CRI): ≥80 min; ≥90 if accurate color is important.
- Dimmability and dim type (forward-phase, TRIAC, or compatible with LED dimmers) — verify compatibility.
- Flicker specs or percent flicker (lower is better) if occupants are sensitive.
- Adjustable arm/head and focused beam for task lighting.
- Warranty and rated lifetime (e.g., L70 25,000–50,000 hours).
- Extras as needed: built-in USB charging, occupancy sensor, smart controls.

Evidence and what I’ve assumed
- Energy savings example (illustrative):
  - 60 W incandescent vs 10 W LED (approx. same usable light):
    - Use 8 hours/day × 365 days = 2,920 hours/year.
    - Incandescent: 60 W × 2,920 h = 175.2 kWh/year (~$26.28 at $0.15/kWh).
    - LED: 10 W × 2,920 h = 29.2 kWh/year (~$4.38 at $0.15/kWh).
    - Annual savings ≈ 146 kWh and ≈ $21.90 per lamp.
  - This shows how lower wattage + similar lumen output yields energy and cost savings. (Adjust numbers for your local electricity rate and actual lamp wattage.)
- General LED performance claims (higher lm/W, long life) are well-supported industry-wide, but specific product claims (e.g., Meadowlight Lamp uses X watts, produces Y lumens, is ENERGY STAR certified) must be verified on product data sheets or manufacturer/ENERGY STAR listings.

Claims that require verification (for any specific lamp)
- Any statement that a given model is ENERGY STAR certified.
- Manufacturer wattage, lumen output and resulting lm/W.
- Dimmability compatibility and percent flicker/flicker-free claims.
- Actual CCT and CRI values.
- Rated lifetime and warranty terms.
- Presence and behavior of sensors or smart features.

Catalog note
- I found an item named “Meadowlight Lamp” in the catalog memory. I don’t have provenance or spec details for it in memory, so I can’t confirm whether it meets ENERGY STAR or the lm/W / CRI / dimming criteria above. That item should be checked against its spec sheet.

If you want, I can:
- Pull the Meadowlight Lamp spec sheet (if it’s in your catalog) and compare it to the checklist above.
- Search your catalog for other ENERGY STAR desk/task LED lamps and produce a short ranked list (efficiency, lumen output, price, warranty).
Tell me which you prefer: I’ll search the catalog for matching models, or if you share budget/appearance preferences, I’ll tailor recommendations.
